blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Jeremiah distinguishes divine speech, prophetic first-person speech, Baruch's scribal role, prose narration, royal and priestly speech, competing prophets, communal voices, nations, and personified Daughter Zion or Judah. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

A literary feature to notice is that Jeremiah uses siege, wound, tears, maternal bodies, non-burial, creation undone, imprisonment, displacement, and fractured memory to represent catastrophe and survival. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. Interpretations differ on some details.
